title: Nguyễn dynasty
capsule: The Nguyễn dynasty was founded when Nguyễn Ánh, having defeated the Tây Sơn rebels with French-supported forces, proclaimed himself Emperor Gia Long at Huế in 1802, unifying Vietnam for the first time under a single administration stretching from the Chinese border to the Gulf of Thailand. His son Minh Mạng (r. 1820–1841) centralized the bureaucracy on a Chinese Confucian model, persecuted Catholic missionaries, and incorporated Cambodia as a protectorate in 1835. French military pressure escalating from 1858 forced the dynasty into a series of concessions: the Treaty of Saigon in 1862 ceded three southern provinces, and subsequent agreements culminating in 1884 reduced the remaining Vietnamese polity to a French protectorate, ending effective Nguyễn sovereignty though the dynasty retained ceremonial status until Emperor Bảo Đại abdicated on August 25, 1945.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Nguyễn core territory is well documented in Vietnamese and French colonial administrative records; the dataset's end date of 1885 reflects the effective loss of sovereignty rather than dynastic extinction, which occurred in 1945.
